answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded web of trust: to join the voyage, each new identity locks a real stake and gathers vouches from already-trusted peers who anchor their standing to a shared ledger. Fake identities can only whisper to one another, so they never collect independent vouches, and any detected duplicate has its bond slashed. The attacker must fund every fake account up front and forfeits the whole stake once caught, so flooding the network costs far more than honest agents can ever earn.
